methodologyNotes: The roster covers 13 distinct mesh Wi-Fi systems spanning Wi-Fi 6 through Wi-Fi 7, drawn from high-search consumer models in 2022-2025. Specs were re-verified against manufacturer product/spec pages (eero.com, store.google.com, netgear.com, tp-link.com, asus.com, store.ui.com / techspecs.ui.com) and corroborated by review outlets (Dong Knows Tech, Tom's Guide, Tom's Hardware, Android Central, BroadbandNow). max_speed_gbps reflects the manufacturer's aggregate theoretical Wi-Fi throughput across all bands. dedicated_backhaul is true ONLY when a radio band or wired path is reserved exclusively for node-to-node communication per the strict definition; mesh systems that use adaptive/dynamic backhaul where every band remains available to clients (eero TrueMesh, Google Nest Wifi Pro) are marked false even though they backhaul wirelessly. coverage_sqft_per_pack is the manufacturer's stated figure for the noted pack size. Prices are the published US price for the exact config named as of access. accessedAt 2026-06-19. Adversarial corrections this pass: eero Pro 6E / eero Max 7 / Google Nest Wifi Pro dedicated_backhaul true->false (no band reserved exclusively); Deco BE85 coverage 7500->9600 sq ft and release 2023-05->2023-04; Orbi RBK763S price null->399.99 (published US price confirmed). All 13 products exist and were retained.

products.name: Amazon eero 6+
products.provenance: Verified from eero.com and eero blog: dual-band Wi-Fi 6 (2.4/5 GHz, 160 MHz in 5 GHz), wired/wireless speeds up to ~1 Gbps, two auto-sensing gigabit Ethernet ports per unit, 4,500 sq ft for 3-pack. Launch MSRP $299.99 (3-pack). Released March 2022 alongside eero Pro 6E per eero's own launch announcement. Dual-band with no exclusively reserved backhaul band -> dedicated_backhaul false (unchanged).

products.name: Amazon eero Pro 6E
products.provenance: Verified from eero.com: tri-band Wi-Fi 6E (2.4/5/6 GHz, 160 MHz), network speeds up to 2.3 Gbps, one 2.5 GbE + one 1 GbE port per unit, 6,000 sq ft (3-pack). eero.com shop page shows 3-pack list $449.99 marked down to $329.99 (current price confirmed via Best Buy/SlickDeals) - price and priceNote retained as accurate. CORRECTED dedicated_backhaul true->false: eero/Help and reviews (BroadbandNow, Android Central) confirm the 6 GHz band is NOT reserved as a dedicated backhaul - all three bands remain available to clients and backhaul is adaptive (TrueMesh), so it does not meet the 'reserved exclusively' definition. Released March 2022.

products.name: Amazon eero Max 7
products.provenance: Verified from eero.com and TechCrunch: tri-band Wi-Fi 7 (2.4/5/6 GHz), wireless up to 4.3 Gbps, wired up to 9.4 Gbps. Each unit has two 10 GbE + two 2.5 GbE = 4 ports. 3-pack covers 7,500 sq ft (2,500 sq ft/unit). $599.99 per unit / $1,699.99 3-pack confirmed via Newegg/eero. Available Oct 26, 2023. CORRECTED dedicated_backhaul true->false: eero uses adaptive multi-band/MLO backhaul with no band reserved exclusively for node-to-node traffic, so it does not meet the strict definition.

products.name: Google Nest Wifi Pro
products.provenance: Verified via Google Store specs and Google Home support: AXE5400 tri-band Wi-Fi 6E (2.4/5/6 GHz), combined up to 5.4 Gbps, 2 Ethernet ports per unit (both 1 GbE). ~2,200 sq ft/unit, 6,600 sq ft for 3-pack. $199.99 single / $399.99 3-pack confirmed. Released Oct 27, 2022. CORRECTED dedicated_backhaul true->false: Google support explicitly states there is no dedicated wireless backhaul channel; the system uses shared bands or wired Ethernet backhaul, so no band is reserved exclusively.

products.name: Netgear Orbi RBK763S
products.priceNote: US price ~$399.99 (Costco-channel RBK763S, listed $399.97 at Costco)
products.provenance: Specs verified from Netgear product page: AX5400 tri-band Wi-Fi 6, up to 5.4 Gbps, 7,500 sq ft (3-pack), genuine dedicated 5 GHz backhaul radio (true). ~3 gigabit ports per unit (averaged across router + 2 satellites). CORRECTED priceUsd null->399.99: the draft set price null claiming no published US price, but the RBK763S is sold through Costco at $399.97 / ~$399.99 MSRP (a published US price), so null was overly conservative. Released September 2022.

products.name: Netgear Orbi 970 (RBE973S)
products.provenance: Verified from Netgear product page (loads, describes RBE973 family) and Tom's Hardware: BE27000 quad-band Wi-Fi 7 (2.4/5GHz-1/5GHz-2/6GHz), up to 27 Gbps, 10,000 sq ft (3-pack), dedicated backhaul (true). ~5 ports/unit averaged (router 6 ports incl. 10G WAN+10G LAN+4x2.5G; satellites 3 ports each). Current price $1,799.99 confirmed (reduced from $1,999.99). Launch November 2023, original MSRP $2,299.99. Source URL uses the netgear.com rbe973sb path (loads and topical).

products.name: TP-Link Deco XE75
products.provenance: Verified from TP-Link US product page and Tom's Guide: AXE5400 tri-band Wi-Fi 6E (2.4/5/6 GHz), 5,400 Mbps combined, three auto-sensing gigabit Ethernet ports per unit (standard XE75), 7,200 sq ft (3-pack), 6 GHz available for configurable backhaul (retained true; standard XE75 backhaul is adaptive but TP-Link advertises 6 GHz backhaul). Current 3-pack street price ~$219.99. Source URL corrected to the canonical tp-link.com product-family path. Released 2022.

products.name: TP-Link Deco BE85
products.provenance: Verified from TP-Link and Dong Knows Tech: BE22000 tri-band Wi-Fi 7 (2.4/5/6 GHz), ~22 Gbps combined (1,376+8,640+11,520 Mbps; draft's 21.5 retained as a conservative aggregate). Each unit: 2x 10G (one RJ45, one SFP+/RJ45 combo) + 2x 2.5G = 4 ports. Supports wired/wireless backhaul (true). MSRP $1,299.99 for 3-pack confirmed. CORRECTED coverage_sqft_per_pack 7500->9600 (TP-Link/Amazon/retailer 3-pack figure is 9,600 sq ft, not 7,500). CORRECTED releaseDate 2023-05->2023-04 (shipped April 14, 2023, as the first Wi-Fi 7 mesh kit).

products.name: ASUS ZenWiFi XT9
products.provenance: Verified via ASUS product page and B&H/Amazon: AX7800 tri-band Wi-Fi 6 (2.4 GHz 574 + 5GHz-1 2402 + 5GHz-2 4804 = 7,780 Mbps ~7.8 Gbps). Each unit: 1x 2.5G WAN + 3x 1G LAN = 4 ports. 2-pack covers 5,700 sq ft. Dedicated 5GHz-2 backhaul band (true). Released June 2022; 2-pack launch MSRP $449.99 (current street ~$300). Specs match draft.

products.name: ASUS ZenWiFi BT10
products.provenance: Verified via ASUS product page and Dong Knows Tech: tri-band Wi-Fi 7 (2.4/5/6 GHz), up to 18 Gbps (688+5,764+11,529 Mbps). Each unit: 1x 10G WAN/LAN + 1x 10G LAN = 2 ports. 2-pack covers 6,000 sq ft. Supports configurable dedicated backhaul (true). Available July 1, 2024 per ASUS press release. 2-pack MSRP ~$849.99 confirmed across Best Buy/Tom's Hardware (cleaned up the draft's confusing per-unit note).

products.name: Ubiquiti UniFi Express (UX)
products.provenance: Verified from Ubiquiti tech-specs and UI community release: dual-band Wi-Fi 6 (2.4 GHz 573.5 Mbps + 5 GHz 2.4 Gbps ~ 2.97 Gbps combined), 1x 1G WAN + 1x 1G LAN = 2 ports. Single unit covers ~1,500 sq ft (140 m2), 50+ clients. Launched November 2023 at $149. dedicated_backhaul false (single-unit gateway/AP). Specs match draft.

products.name: Ubiquiti UniFi Express 7 (UX7)
products.provenance: Verified from Ubiquiti tech-specs and US store: 6-stream tri-radio Wi-Fi 7 (2.4 GHz 688 Mbps + 5 GHz 4.3 Gbps + 6 GHz 5.7 Gbps ~ 10.7 Gbps), 1x 10G WAN + 1x 2.5G LAN = 2 ports. Covers ~1,750 sq ft (160 m2). $199 confirmed at Ubiquiti US store. Released February 2025. dedicated_backhaul false (single unit). Specs match draft.

products.name: TP-Link Deco X55
products.provenance: Verified from TP-Link product family page and Amazon listing: AX3000 dual-band Wi-Fi 6 (2.4 GHz 574 Mbps + 5 GHz 2,402 Mbps = 3 Gbps combined), three gigabit Ethernet ports per unit, supports Ethernet (wired) backhaul but no exclusively reserved wireless backhaul band -> dedicated_backhaul false. 3-pack covers 6,500 sq ft. Launched January 2022 (~$279.99); current ~$179.99. Replaced dead/uncertain HighSpeedInternet corroboration with an Amazon product listing; source URL corrected to canonical tp-link.com product-family path.
